title: Comparing
intro: Turkmen adjectives don't change to say **bigger** or **the biggest**. The thing you compare with goes in the ablative: *Merdan Batyrdan uzyn*, Merdan is taller than Batyr, literally **tall from Batyr**. *has* means **more**, the suffix `-rAk` **-er** or **a bit more**, and *iň* **the most**. This unit adds **as … as** (*ýaly*, *deň*), the words that make an adjective stronger or weaker, the doubled colours (*ap-ak*, *gap-gara*), and adjectives used as adverbs: *gowy gürleýär*, she speaks well.

blocks.text: To compare two things, put the second one in the ablative, `-dAn` ([A1 unit 7](a1-u07)), and keep the adjective as it is: *Merdan Batyrdan uzyn*, Merdan is taller than Batyr. *Aşgabat Marydan uly*, Ashgabat is bigger than Mary. With a pronoun, the ablative pronoun: *Sen menden uzyn*, you're taller than me.

items.en: In winter Daşoguz is colder than Ashgabat.

blocks.text: **has** means **more** and goes right before the adjective: *has uly*, bigger; *has gowy*, better; *has gyzykly*, more interesting. With a `-dAn` phrase it makes the difference stronger, like **even**: *Aşgabat Marydan has uly*. On its own it compares with something already known: *Bu kitap has gyzykly*, this book is more interesting.

**-rAk** is a suffix: *-rak* after back vowels, *-räk* after front ones, with *ä* like `-ýAr`. It means **-er** or **a bit more**, often without saying than what: *Bu otag ulurak*, this room is bigger; *Howa salkynrak*, it's a bit cooler. After *uly* and *gowy*, the *y* rounds before it by the rule of [A1 unit 3](a1-u03): *ulurak*, *gowurak*.
The two can meet: *Merdan Batyrdan uzynrak* is also right. To ask which of two is bigger: *Haýsy otag uly?*, which room is bigger? Turkmen needs no special word: the question and the context compare.

blocks.title: -dan on the second thing
blocks.text: The ablative goes on what you compare **with**: *Merdan Batyrdan uzyn*, Merdan is taller than Batyr. Move it to the other name and the meaning flips: *Batyr Merdandan uzyn*, Batyr is taller than Merdan. And *has* is a separate word before the adjective: *has gowy*, not `gowyhas`.
Put *iň* before the adjective: *iň uly*, the biggest; *iň gowy*, the best; *iň köp*, the most; *iň erbet*, the worst. *Bu iň gowy palaw*, this is the best pilaf.

**The biggest of a group** uses the possessive construction of [A1 unit 10](a1-u10): the group in the genitive, *iň* and the adjective, and the noun with its third-person ending. *Türkmenistanyň iň uly şäheri*, the biggest city of Turkmenistan; *synpyň iň uzyn okuwçysy*, the tallest pupil in the class. Or say where, with the locative: *synpda iň uzyn*, the tallest in the class.

items.en: Ashgabat is the biggest city in Turkmenistan.
The Karakum is the biggest desert in Turkmenistan.
The Caspian is the biggest lake in the world.
Who is the tallest in the class?

blocks.text: Another way to say **the most** is to compare with everyone, *hemmeden*: *Ol hemmeden uzyn*, she is taller than everyone, the tallest of all. *hemme* is the word for **all, everyone** of [A2 unit 5](a2-u05).

blocks.title: Water and land
blocks.text: *Hazar deňzi*, the Caspian Sea, is called a sea in Turkmen and in English, but it is the largest lake on Earth, so *Hazar dünýäniň iň uly köli* is right too. Its coast is in [A2 unit 7](a2-u07-culture), where *küştdepdi* is at home.

sections.title: As … as, very, a bit: ýaly, deň and the intensifiers

blocks.text: *ýaly* means **like, as**. It follows the noun: *gar ýaly ak*, white as snow; *kakasy ýaly uzyn*, as tall as his father. After a personal pronoun it takes the genitive: *meniň ýaly*, like me; *seniň ýaly*, like you; *onuň ýaly*, like him, like that.

items.en: He is as tall as his father.
This bread is as white as snow.

blocks.text: *meňzemek*, **to look like**, says the same with a verb, and takes the dative: *Aýna ejesine meňzeýär*. *ejesine* is *eje* + *-si* + the pronominal *n* + *-e*, as in [A1 unit 10](a1-u10).

*deň* means **equal, the same** in size, height or amount. What it is equal to takes *bilen*: *Bu otag ol otag bilen deň*, this room is the same size as that one. For height, use *boý*: *Merdanyň boýy Batyryň boýy bilen deň*, Merdan is as tall as Batyr, literally **Merdan's height is equal with Batyr's height**.
They go before the adjective, and also before a comparative: *birneme ulurak*, a bit bigger; *örän gowy*, very good. *azajyk* also works with a verb: *Azajyk garaş!*, wait a little!

blocks.title: ýaly after a pronoun
blocks.text: With a pronoun, *ýaly* wants the genitive: *seniň ýaly*, *meniň ýaly*. With a noun, the noun stays as it is: *gar ýaly*, *Aýna ýaly*.

For **completely, perfectly**, some adjectives, mostly colours, double their first syllable. Take the word up to its first vowel, add a consonant, put a hyphen, then the whole word: *ak* → *ap-ak*, pure white; *gara* → *gap-gara*, jet black. The added consonant is usually *p*, but not always, so learn each one.

items.en: It snowed; everything is pure white.
In spring the gardens are lush green.
This road goes straight to Mary.

blocks.title: Don't invent them
blocks.text: Only some adjectives double, and each has its own consonant: *göm-gök* with *m*, *gös-göni* with *s*. Use the ones you have met, and say *örän* for the rest: *örän uly*, not `up-uly`. The hyphen is part of the spelling.

sections.title: Well, fast, slowly: adjectives as adverbs

blocks.text: An adjective can describe how something is done, with no ending: just put it before the verb. *gowy* is **good** and **well**: *Ol türkmençe gowy gürleýär*, she speaks Turkmen well. *çalt* is **fast** and **quickly**: *Çalt gel!*, come quickly! You met *Haýal aýdyň*, speak slowly, in [A1 unit 12](a1-u12).
Comparing works the same way: *has çalt*, faster; *gowurak*, better; *iň gowy*, best: *Kim iň çalt ylgaýar?*, who runs fastest?

**Doubled adverbs.** Some adverbs are said twice, with a hyphen, for something that goes on step by step: *ýuwaş-ýuwaş*, slowly, little by little, gently. *Ýuwaş-ýuwaş öwrenýärin*, I'm learning little by little.

blocks.title: No -ly
blocks.text: English turns **quick** into **quickly**. Turkmen uses the adjective as it is: *çalt* is both. The place before the verb shows that it describes the action.

summary: **Than**: the second thing in `-dAn`: *Merdan Batyrdan uzyn*; *Sen menden uzyn*.
*has* (more) before the adjective: *has uly*; `-rAk` (-er, a bit more): *ulurak*, *kiçiräk*, *gowurak*.
**The most**: *iň*: *iň uly*; *Türkmenistanyň iň uly şäheri*; *hemmeden uzyn*, the tallest of all.
**Like, as**: *ýaly* after a noun (*gar ýaly ak*) or a genitive pronoun (*seniň ýaly*); *deň*, the same, with *bilen*.
Adjectives as adverbs before the verb: *gowy gürleýär*, *çalt sürýär*; *ýuwaş-ýuwaş*, little by little.
